title: Web-first assertions & auto-waiting
summary: await expect(locator).toBeVisible()/toHaveText()/toHaveCount() retry until true or until the expect timeout (5 s by default).
why: Pages load asynchronously. A check that reads the DOM once (isVisible(), textContent(), count()) races the app; a web-first assertion waits for the expected state, so it is reliable without sleeps.
body:
Web-first (async, retrying): toBeVisible, toBeHidden, toHaveText, toContainText, toHaveValue, toBeChecked, toHaveCount, toHaveAttribute, toHaveURL, toHaveTitle, toHaveScreenshot, toMatchAriaSnapshot, toBeOK.
Generic (sync, no retry): toBe, toEqual, toContain, toMatchObject — use them on plain values (API JSON).

expect.soft() records a failure but continues; expect.poll() retries any function; expect(...).toPass() retries a block. Never use page.waitForTimeout() in a real test.
objectives: Pick a web-first matcher for a UI check
Know when generic matchers are fine
teachAlong: The orders API answers after 250–1600 ms.
toHaveCount keeps re-checking until 3 items exist.
